title: After a quarantine lift, a remote runner acts on requests queued before the quarantine without the requester confirming them
outcome: When a satellite's link returns after a quarantine or outage, the messages queued during it reach the recipient marked with their age and the outage they waited through. Runner guidance or tooling requires a requester's confirmation before starting expensive work from such a backlog, so superseded runs are not started.
acceptance: Delivery after a link recovery exposes, per message, its creation time and that it was queued across an outage, through the supported mailbox read surface.

The runner protocol (documentation and any runner helper) requires confirming a request older than the outage with its requester before launching it, and a test or documented drill shows a pre-outage request is held rather than started.
